content.text: KÃ¶nigrufen (Call the King) is the 'queen of card games' in Austria. It is a 4-player Tarot game with a 54-card deck. The defining feature is the 'calling' mechanic where a declarer chooses a partner by calling a King suit. There are numerous contracts ranging from simple games to complex negative bids (Bettel) and high-value solos.

The Tarock family emerged in Northern Italy during the Early Renaissance (first evidenced 1440). From the mid-18th century in the German-speaking world and Habsburg monarchy, reforms added bidding (from L'Hombre and Quadrille), the 54-card pack, talon exchange, and the bonus when the lowest trump (Trump I) wins the last trick. Königrufen first appears in 1827 as a four-player variant of Tapp Tarock in an appendix to the Tarok Tappen rulebook; the first book devoted solely to Königrufen was published in Vienna in 1840. The game boomed between 1880 and 1920 and gained more contracts throughout the 20th century. It is played across Austria and South Tyrol and by 2015 had become the favourite card game of Austrians.
